decisions.executionNote: Basket is in left workspace. Raise left wrist and begin a gradual downward-facing approach, preserving elbow-up continuity.
Move above the left basket and progressively pitch the open gripper toward a top-down egg grasp.
Align left gripper over the rear egg; finish top-down rotation while approaching slowly above basket rim.
Use head geometry and wrist view to center the rear egg, descending with the fingers open.

Lift the closed grasp clear of the basket, then begin carrying toward the holder; check egg retention in the next RGB view.

Approach the holder's left rear cup from the left, reducing height gradually while maintaining the retained egg.
Fine-align the egg over the left rear socket by a small wrist tilt and controlled descent; keep the left wrist on its own side.

Lower the retained egg into the rear-left cup with small steps, keeping the wrist clear of the lid.
Seat the first egg a little lower, open the gripper over the rear-left cup, and retreat upward to verify placement.

Approach the rightmost remaining egg in the left basket with open fingers, then use the wrist view for final alignment.
The open outer finger appears near the basket rim. Shift inward before lowering further to center the second egg.
The wrist did not follow the inward move, suggesting rim contact. Lift clear and slightly narrow the empty gripper before repositioning.
With the rim cleared, lower the narrower open gripper over the rightmost basket egg, staying slightly inward.
Lower around the second egg, close fully, and make a short vertical lift to check retention.
Lift the second egg clear and carry it toward the front-left socket, gradually restoring the successful placement tilt.
Carry the visibly retained second egg to the front-left cup, slowing near the holder and keeping the wrist left of center.
Fine-align and lower the second egg over the front-left socket, retaining it until the placement depth is verified.
The second egg has shifted lower in the fingers. Nudge it over the front-left cup, release, and lift away to inspect.
Two eggs are visibly in the left sockets. Withdraw above the basket to acquire a remaining egg, maintaining clearance.
Move above the left of the two remaining basket eggs, with partially open fingers to avoid catching the rim.
Center the third egg between the fingers while descending slowly into the left basket.
Close on the centered third egg and lift clear of the basket, checking that only one egg is retained.
The third egg was not retained and shifted toward the basket front. Reopen and realign above its new position before a deeper grasp.
Rim contact displaced the egg again. Lift off the rim, shift inward over the egg, then resume a centered descent.
The third egg is now centered. Lower open fingers well around its sides before closing, watching for rim interference.
The egg sits forward of the grasp axis. Track its new position toward the robot, close around its sides, and test a short lift.
Lift vertically with the gripper closed to verify the third egg is retained before moving toward the holder.
Third egg is visibly retained. Carry toward the holder and tilt the fingertips toward the empty right column while keeping the left wrist left of center.
The third egg slipped onto the table. Reopen, restore the near-vertical grasp, and approach its visible resting position for recovery.
Track the settled table egg with open fingers and descend to a lower grasp height, now unobstructed by the basket rim.
Close the centered recovery grasp without pushing lower into the tabletop, then lift vertically and inspect retention.
Recovery grasp missed. Reopen fully and approach the newly settled egg from directly above, removing the forward tilt before a deeper grasp.
Clear the basket rim and allow the empty gripper to finish opening before the next recovery descent.
Reorient the open fingers along the basket edge, rather than across its rim, while centering over the table egg.
Finish rotating the fingers parallel to the rim and descend above the table egg, avoiding lateral contact with the basket.
Replan after the continuity rejection: clear the rim by moving the wrist outward and pitching the fingertips toward the egg with smaller rotation increments.
The wrist view still aims at the basket edge. Translate the open gripper outward and toward the robot to bring the loose egg into the grasp view.
Use the now-visible loose egg to correct the grasp center while descending, with fingers aligned to clear the basket edge.
Correct away from rim contact toward the visible loose egg, close at the current depth, and test a small lift.
The loose egg remains ahead of the closed fingertips. Reopen and make a smaller visual alignment correction before attempting closure again.
Approach the loose egg obliquely from outside the basket: offset the wrist outward while tipping the fingers inward to improve rim clearance.
Keep the wrist outside the rim and correct the fingertip pitch toward the loose egg, using small rotation increments.
Advance the fingertips slightly toward and down around the loose egg, narrowing the opening for rim clearance, then close.
Lift slowly to reveal whether the grasp retained the loose egg or contacted the basket rim; the wrist view is occluded.
Move the closed grasp up and away from the basket edge to distinguish retained egg from rim contact and regain a clear view.
The egg is now outside the rim. Reopen fully and align over its latest table position without changing the wrist orientation.
Descend around the centered loose egg with the gripper fully open; the egg is now clear enough of the rim for a deeper grasp.
Close at the deeper grasp height and lift vertically; judge egg retention from the next head and wrist views rather than aperture state.

Carry the retained third egg above the holder, progressively aiming the fingertips toward the empty right column while the left wrist stays left of center.
Position the third egg over the rear-right cup using a gentle inward fingertip tilt, keeping clearance above the two placed eggs.
Lower the retained third egg into the rear-right socket with small translation steps and fixed grasp orientation.

Three eggs are visible in the holder. Withdraw toward the final basket egg and gradually restore the earlier downward grasp orientation.
Approach above the last egg and continue restoring the downward grasp; keep clearance from the basket until orientation is established.
Finish the near-vertical grasp orientation and lower over the last basket egg, with a modest opening to clear the rim.
Center the last egg between the fingers, descend around its sides, close fully, and begin a short retention lift.
Lift the final egg clear with a fixed grasp orientation and begin a slow carry toward the remaining socket.

Bring the last egg above the front-right cup while keeping the left wrist on its side of center and maintaining the closed grasp.
Fine-align the last egg over the empty front-right cup and lower gradually while preserving the grasp and avoiding the other eggs.
Seat the fourth egg slightly inward and lower in the front-right cup, then open the fingers and start a gentle withdrawal.
Withdraw from the fourth egg to inspect its seating, then close the empty fingers and begin orienting for a controlled lid push.
All four eggs are visible in their sockets. Move the closed fingertips above and behind the upright lid edge for a gentle forward-closing push.
The lid is contacting the fingers. Guide its upper edge toward the robot and slightly downward with a gradual hinge-following rotation.
The lid has started folding forward. Continue guiding its upper edge along the closing arc with small downward and toward-robot motion.
Release the lid edge now that it is tilted forward, then withdraw clear so it can settle closed without being trapped between the fingers.
